newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Cardenas accused of nepotism.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Cardenas accused of nepotism.

text.p: Five months before taking office, Mexico City's popular mayor-elect Cuauhtemoc Cardenas was embroiled on Wednesday in his first scandal after he named his son as a possible member of his future cabinet.

Charges of nepotism were splashed over the front pages of Mexican newspapers after Cardenas appointed his son, Cuauhtemoc Cardenas Batel, to a key six-person team to ensure a smooth handover of power on Dec. 5.
At a news conference after meeting with the capital's outgoing mayor Oscar Espinosa on Tuesday, Cardenas said there was "no doubt at all" the six collaborators would form part of his cabinet.
But after reporters raised questions of nepotism, the left-wing leader was later forced to row back -- even though he complained of "wrongful and fraudulent interpretations" about his son's position.
"Up to now, I've invited nobody to to be a part of the new government," Cardenas said in a statement late Tuesday.
Cardenas Batel also defended himself from charges of string-pulling.
"I don't see where there is nepotism. They are not paying me, I am not being promoted to a public position by a family member," he told reporters.
Cardenas, a member of the Party of the Democratic Revolution, won by a landslide on July 6 the first elections for mayor of Mexico City in modern history.

He is a veteran leftist figure and former member of the ruling Institutional revolutionary Party (PRI), that has ruled Mexico for 68 years. Some critics have worried he will be an old-style populist when in office, though he has pledged to run a modern administration and attack graft.
